question: If every customer gets the same number of rule slots, does a list per group beat one global list?
practical_meaning: Every customer's page has B recommendation slots: should each customer group get its own list, or should everybody see the same store-wide list?
rules: P5 from common.json, V3_combination de-duplication from E10 (unit = combination, skip already-kept and superset combinations)

lists.G: top B combinations of the global ranking; every customer uses it
lists.L: each true group's own top B combinations; a customer uses only their group's list (3B combinations stored, B seen per customer)
lists.random: each random seed's groups build their own top B combinations in the same way (A1 primary, S, A2)

metrics: coverage (order) and customer-macro coverage, overall and per group
per group: coverage of the group's orders by its own list vs by G's list
Discovery descriptions: Jaccard of each group's list with G's list, #combinations not in G's top B, joint count of the last selected combination, group basket count
comparisons: L - G with paired customer bootstrap interval
L position in the A1 / S / A2 distributions (empirical p)

periods.discovery: build lists and describe them; in-sample coverage for reference only
periods.test: later single run; primary hypothesis H_E9 at B=100

interpretation_rules.group_lists_help: L-G interval above 0 AND L above the A1 95th percentile (empirical p <= 0.05)
interpretation_rules.help_from_any_split: L-G interval above 0 but L not above the A1 95th percentile
